title: Fuse two ranked lists
summary: Reciprocal rank fusion combines ranked lists without comparing their raw scores. Each list contributes 1 / (k + rank) for a document it ranks, and documents absent from a list contribute nothing from it.
example: With k = 60, a document ranked first in one list and third in another scores 1/61 + 1/63.
takeaway: Fusion can only reorder documents some retriever already found; a document in no list scores nothing.
instruction: Given lists (an array of ID arrays, each ordered best first) and a positive integer k, return the IDs ordered by descending fused score, where a list contributes 1 / (k + rank) using zero-based rank. Break ties by the order a document first appears, scanning lists in order and positions within a list in order. Return an empty array when there are no lists.
hint: Accumulate a score per ID and remember where each ID was first seen. Sort by score descending, then by first appearance ascending.

tests.label: Documents in both lists outrank documents in one
A single list keeps its order
Ties fall back to first appearance
A smaller constant sharpens the top rank
